constraint.rule: no file may depend on bytes
constraint.interpreted_by: caller: --dependency takes a package name, this tool does not read prose

known_blind_spots.statement: A call made through an interface is resolved to the interface, not to the implementation that runs.
known_blind_spots.implication: A file whose only route to the prohibited dependency runs through an interface can be reported SAFE. Check implementations of any interface the invalidated files satisfy.

known_blind_spots.statement: Reflective and dynamically constructed calls leave no edge in a static parse.
known_blind_spots.implication: Code that reaches bytes by name at runtime is invisible here. Grep for the string form of the dependency as well.

known_blind_spots.statement: Generated files are classified from their committed content, and the generator that produced them is not analysed.
known_blind_spots.implication: A generator that emits the prohibited dependency will reintroduce it after any hand fix. Fix the generator, then regenerate.

known_blind_spots.statement: SAFE means no path was found in this snapshot. It is not proof of absence.
known_blind_spots.implication: Do not report the constraint satisfied on the strength of a SAFE verdict alone. Satisfaction is demonstrated by the validation commands, not by this classification.

known_blind_spots.statement: Files in inventory-only languages are parsed for structure but not for relations, so they carry no verdict at all.
known_blind_spots.implication: Every UNREACHED item is an open question. Treating the SAFE count as the whole remainder undercounts the work.

known_blind_spots.statement: The prohibited dependency is matched on the import path as written, exactly or as a path prefix.
known_blind_spots.implication: A dependency reached under an alias, a re-export, or a differently spelled module path is not matched. Confirm the name is the one this repository actually writes.

evidence.reason: import declaration matched by language-specific scanner

agent_instructions: Open regexp.go and read the code around each evidence line before editing.
Remove the dependency on bytes, or replace it with an approved equivalent that provides the same behaviour.
Do not defeat the check by aliasing the import or moving the call behind a wrapper in the same repository: the dependency would still be present, and the next run would report the wrapper instead.
acceptance_criteria: A re-run of the pivot command no longer lists regexp.go as INVALIDATED.
`go build ./...` succeeds.
`go test .` passes.

agent_instructions: Do not edit mux.go first. It breaks no rule on its own; it is here because it depends on regexp.go.
After regexp.go is fixed, re-read this file's use of it and adjust only what the fix actually changed.
If the root fix kept the same interface, the correct outcome for this file is no diff at all.
acceptance_criteria: `go test .` passes after the root fix has landed.
A re-run of the pivot command reports mux.go as SAFE, or the remaining edge is explained in the report.

notes: Run every required command. A plan is complete when the commands pass, not when the edits look right.
Re-running the pivot command is what proves the constraint is satisfied: the invalidated count must reach zero.

must_not_claim: Must not claim bytes has been removed without re-running the pivot command and showing the invalidated count at zero.
Must not claim any test passes without having executed it and read the result.
Must not present a SAFE verdict as proof that no dependency path exists; it means none was found in this snapshot.
Must not count an UNREACHED file as resolved. It was never analysed for relations.
Must not report the plan complete while any P0 item is open, regardless of how many P1 and P2 items were closed.
Must not silently widen the plan: a file that is not a work item here has not been assessed for this change.
must_do: Work P0 items before P1: an at-risk file cannot be verified until the root it depends on is fixed.
Cite the work item id in each commit so the plan and the history stay linked.
Re-run the pivot command after the edits and attach the new counts to the report.
